title: Adic quotient cohomology of a finite short complex has the completed cohomology as limit
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $U\xrightarrow{u}V\xrightarrow{v}W$ a short complex of finitely generated $A$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], meaning $vu=0$. Put $H=\ker(v)/\operatorname{im}(u)$. For $n\geq1$, let $u_n,v_n$ be the induced maps on the quotients by $I^n$ and put $H_n=\ker(v_n)/\operatorname{im}(u_n)$. Give $(H_n)$ the transitions induced by the quotient maps. The canonical maps $H/I^nH\to H_n$, sending the class of a cycle to its class modulo $I^nV$, induce an $A$-linear isomorphism
$$\varprojlim_{n\geq1}H/I^nH\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}H_n.$$
Here each inverse limit is the module of compatible sequences, and the limit on the left is the module adic completion, defined by this compatible-sequence formula. The isomorphism is natural for all triples of $A$-linear maps between such short complexes commuting with $u,v$.

source.place: Tag 0EGU (lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees), assertion (2), with the canonical maps preceding the enumeration; naturality is induced by the displayed cycle maps.

proof.text: Write $Z=\ker v$, $B=\operatorname{im}u$, and $P_n=v^{-1}(I^nW)$. Since $vu=0$, $B+I^nV\subseteq P_n$, and lifting representatives gives $H_n=P_n/(B+I^nV)$. Also $H/I^nH=Z/(B+I^nZ)$: the image of $I^nZ$ in $Z/B$ is $I^nH$ by expanding finite sums of ideal multiples. Thus inclusion $Z\subseteq P_n$ defines $\phi_n:H/I^nH\to H_n$. Inclusion of the numerator and denominator submodules for $m\geq n$ defines all transition maps. Both routes in each transition square send a representative $z$ to its class at level $n$; hence $(\phi_n)$ induces the stated linear map $\Phi$ on compatible sequences.

source.place: Tag 0EGU (lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees), proof of (2) and preceding construction of the maps psi_n.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to $v(V)\subseteq W$ and $Z\subseteq V$. Its hypotheses hold because $A$ is Noetherian and the ambient modules $W,V$ are finite. Obtain $a,b\geq0$ with $v(V)\cap I^nW\subseteq I^{n-a}v(V)$ for $n\geq a$ and $Z\cap I^rV\subseteq I^{r-b}Z$ for $r\geq b$. Set $c=a+b+1$. If $y\in P_n$ and $n\geq c$, the first inclusion gives $v(y)\in I^{n-a}v(V)=v(I^{n-a}V)$. The equality follows by writing an element as a finite sum of ideal multiples and lifting each image term to $V$. Choose $w\in I^{n-a}V$ with $v(w)=v(y)$; then $z=y-w\in Z$.

source.place: Tag 0EGU (lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees), proof of (2) and preceding construction of the maps psi_n.

proof.text: For $n\geq c+1$ define $\psi_n:H_n\to H/I^{n-c}H$ by sending the class of $y=z+w$ from step 2 to the class of $z$. To check independence, let $y'=z'+w'$ represent the same class. Then $y'-y=ut+t_n$ with $t_n\in I^nV$, and $z'-z-ut=t_n+w-w'\in Z\cap I^{n-a}V$. The second bound of step 2 puts this in $I^{n-a-b}Z\subseteq I^{n-c}Z$. Hence $z,z'$ give the same class modulo $B+I^{n-c}Z$. Sums of chosen decompositions and their scalar multiples are decompositions of the sums and scalar multiples, so independence of choices proves that $\psi_n$ is $A$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0EGU (lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees), proof of (2) and preceding construction of the maps psi_n.

proof.text: The maps $\psi_n$ commute with transitions: for $m\geq n\geq c+1$, a decomposition $y=z+w$ at level $m$ is also valid at level $n$, since $I^{m-a}V\subseteq I^{n-a}V$. Both routes therefore send $y$ to the class of $z$ in $H/I^{n-c}H$. Furthermore $\psi_n\phi_n$ is the quotient map $H/I^nH\to H/I^{n-c}H$, by taking $w=0$ for a true cycle. The composite $\phi_{n-c}\psi_n$ is the transition $H_n\to H_{n-c}$, since $y-z=w\in I^{n-a}V\subseteq I^{n-c}V$. These checks use representatives and so assert the equalities of the actual canonical maps.

source.place: Tag 0EGU (lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees), proof of (2) and preceding construction of the maps psi_n.

proof.text: For a compatible sequence $x=(x_n)$ in $(H_n)$, put $\Psi(x)_k=\psi_{k+c}(x_{k+c})$ for every $k\geq1$. Transition compatibility from step 4 makes this a compatible sequence in $(H/I^kH)$, and $\Psi$ is linear. For a compatible sequence $h=(h_n)$ on the left, step 4 gives $(\Psi\Phi h)_k$ equal to the reduction of $h_{k+c}$ at level $k$, namely $h_k$. For $x$ on the right it gives $(\Phi\Psi x)_k$ equal to the transition of $x_{k+c}$ to level $k$, namely $x_k$. Thus $\Psi$ and $\Phi$ are inverse linear maps; no exactness-of-inverse-limit theorem or pro-category identification is needed.

source.place: Tag 0EGU (lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees), proof of (2) and preceding construction of the maps psi_n.

proof.text: For a commuting triple $(f_U,f_V,f_W)$ between the short complexes, $f_V$ sends $Z$ into $Z'$, $B$ into $B'$, $I^nV$ into $I^nV'$, and $P_n$ into $P_n'$: $v'f_V(y)=f_Wv(y)\in I^nW'$ for $y\in P_n$. It therefore induces both maps on quotient cohomology and the map $H/I^nH\to H'/I^nH'$. The square with $\phi_n,\phi_n'$ commutes because each route sends a cycle $z$ to the class of $f_V(z)$. The same representative computation commutes with quotient transitions. Taking compatible sequences gives $f_{\mathrm{right}}\Phi=\Phi'f_{\mathrm{left}}$, the asserted naturality. Multiplication by the inverses gives naturality of the inverse as well, without choosing compatible Artin–Rees constants for different complexes.

lean.statement: theorem finite_short_complex_adic_cohomology_limit {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : Ideal R) : ∃ e : ∀ (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)), Module.Finite R S.X₁ → Module.Finite R S.X₂ → Module.Finite R S.X₃ → AdicCompletion I S.homology ≃ₗ[R] ↥(ModuleCat.sectionsSubmodule (tower I S)), ∀ (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (h₁ : Module.Finite R S.X₁) (h₂ : Module.Finite R S.X₂) (h₃ : Module.Finite R S.X₃), (∀ (x : AdicCompletion I S.homology) (n : ℕ) (h : S.homology), AdicCompletion.eval I S.homology (n + 1) x = (power I S.homology (n + 1)).mkQ h → (e S h₁ h₂ h₃ x).val (op n) = ShortComplex.homologyMap (S.mapNatTrans (projection I (n + 1))) h) ∧ ∀ (T : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (k₁ : Module.Finite R T.X₁) (k₂ : Module.Finite R T.X₂) (k₃ : Module.Finite R T.X₃) (f : S ⟶ T) (x : AdicCompletion I S.homology) (n : ℕ), ShortComplex.homologyMap ((quotient I (n + 1)).mapShortComplex.map f) ((e S h₁ h₂ h₃ x).val (op n)) = (e T k₁ k₂ k₃ (AdicCompletion.map I (ShortComplex.homologyMap f).hom x)).val (op n)
